rule: Derek 2026-10-14 (#6694): a page either auditor calls worse is not written; STOP if Opus calls any worse or Gemini > 4/40

worse.line: B worse (yes/no) (nominal): α —, 40 pages — no pairable units

rows.opus_note: X reads the painting's inscription as printed ('茅簷閒杵臼竹屋細 簸颺照人珠琲光奮…'); Y invents a different poem ('嘉穀既升盤 功需在簸揚…').
rows.gemini_note: Y invents an inscription ('嘉穀既升盤') not present on the leaf, whereas X faithfully transcribes the poem written on the painting ('茅簷閒杵臼竹屋細').

rows.opus_note: X's Greek has sense-changing misreadings that Y gets right as printed ('ἄγγελα δῆριν' for 'ἄγρια', 'ἐθιμόντε' for 'ἰθύνοντα', 'πυθέωσιν' for 'πτολίεσσιν'), and X's Latin has 'Belgicatum' for 'Belgica tum'.
rows.gemini_note: X severely corrupts the Greek text, misreading names such as 'Βασιλείου' as 'Βασιλέως' and 'Βάζκιον' as 'Βάκχιον', and turning multiple lines into gibberish.

rows.opus_note: The body texts agree in substance; Y has small slips ('eratérem', 'cam trado') and cuts the side note down to 'Agenoris filius.', where the print has 'Cadmus Agenoris filius'.
rows.gemini_note: Y corrupts 'catenam' to 'caternam', misreads 'eam' as 'cam', and interpolates 'Cadmum' into the main text.

rows.opus_note: X reads 'magnus ille & spuriæ philosophiæ…spuriæ Deus', repeating 'spuriæ'; the print has 'totius philosophiæ', as Y gives it.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'totius' as 'spuriæ' ('spuriæ philosophiæ') and 'sæculi' as 'fæculi'.

rows.opus_note: Y drops the title 'M. VITRVVII POLLIONIS DE ARCHITECTVRA LIBER SEXTVS. PRAEFATIO.' and puts 'f' where the print has long s ('fperemus'); X records the leaf faithfully.
rows.gemini_note: Y omits the entire heading ('M. VITRVVII POLLIONIS DE ARCHITECTVRA LIBER SEXTVS. PRAEFATIO.').

rows.opus_note: X misreads every C as L, so the gathering references come out as 'L 3' instead of 'C 3' and the chapters as 'La./Lap.'; Y reads them correctly.
rows.gemini_note: X systematically misreads gathering signature C as L, transcribes 'Capitulum' as 'Lapitulum', and misreads 'seminibz' as 'feminibz'.

rows.opus_note: Y follows the printed apparatus (e.g. note a: 'Infra in itin. A. et B. خان روان ut Edrisi… D. خان زوان… E. خاوران ut Djih.-Numa'); X scrambles which manuscripts give which readings in notes a, b and d.
rows.gemini_note: X omits 'E. خاوران' in note a and replaces 'Jacut ديوره' with 'Jacut ربواذه' in note d.

rows.opus_note: The two are nearly identical; Y has 'navigio pertransit' where the print has 'pertransitur'.
rows.gemini_note: Y transcribes 'pertransitur' incorrectly as 'pertransit'.

rows.opus_note: Both give only the ink shelfmark '12. 32. H. 5' and treat the mirrored title page as show-through.
rows.gemini_note: Both transcriptions identically record the only text on this leaf as '->12. 32. H. 5<-' and correctly treat the rest as show-through.

rows.opus_note: Y leaves out passages ('sesquilatera longitudine ad Ciconiæ rostrum, colore'; 'iis, quas Gallinulas aquaticas … Germanis'), reads 'hominem' for 'nomen', and mixes line numbers into the text.
rows.gemini_note: Y omits the clause 'iis, quas Gallinulas aquaticas nostri vocant, auibus Glottidem adnumero, quæ omnes fidipedes sunt. Germanis' and corrupts 'Apitius' to 'Apitem'.

rows.opus_note: Both are close; Y misreads 'ſcilentio' as 'ſcientio', 'ſpiritali' as 'ſpirituali', 'ꝑtinus' as 'pōtinus', and drops the 'q' in 'rūq; q epiſcopatus', none of which changes the sense much.
rows.gemini_note: X faithfully transcribes the leaf, whereas Y introduces spurious macrons ('propriām', 'uiām'), incorrect word divisions ('de primī'), and omits 'q̃' before 'epiſcopatus'.

rows.opus_note: Same body text; X records the woodcut's numbers correctly ('24 · 113 · 8 · 312 · 132 …'), while Y's description adds a circle (show-through) and 'astrological or alchemical symbols' that are not printed.
rows.gemini_note: Y omits the numbers printed in the woodcut diagram ('24', '113', '8', etc.).

rows.opus_note: Verse text identical; X reads the stamp correctly as 'ESCUELA SUPERIOR DE DIPLOMATICA BIBLIOTECA' where Y has 'Escola … Diplomática'.
rows.gemini_note: X correctly transcribes the stamped library text ('ESCUELA SUPERIOR DE DIPLOMATICA BIBLIOTECA'), whereas Y omits it and misspells the name as 'Escola'.

rows.opus_note: Greek text, apparatus and commentary agree word for word; they differ only in layout (Y keeps the 'ap-/poni' column split).
rows.gemini_note: Both transcriptions faithfully record the leaf's text and numbers, differing only in conventions such as layout markup ('<column-break/>') and punctuation ('..' vs '...') that do not affect reading.

rows.opus_note: X keeps the boxed labels ('第二南門金剛…并青色', '第一東門淨地并黄色') separate from '寶生佛身青色' and '阿閦佛身白色'; Y merges them into '第二南門寶生佛身青色', drops the boxed text and invents a margin note, '四門論 向後'.
rows.gemini_note: Y omits the gate inscriptions '金剛淨戒并青色' and '淨地并黄色' from the first two gates.

rows.opus_note: X gives a sound expanded reading, while Y garbles many words ('te uil?' for 'se uilius', 'sheret ho' for 'deberet homo', 'meulet' for 'incubet', 'cũ he auricalcū' for 'cum sit').
rows.gemini_note: Y introduces multiple corruptions and pseudo-words, reading 'vrote' for 'vxorem', 'te' for 'se', and 'meulet' for 'incubet'.

rows.opus_note: Y gives the page number as '380' (the leaf prints 580) and reads 'ſumantur'/'ſumitur' as 'fumantur'/'fumitur', which changes the sense; X matches the page.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads 'sumantur' as 'fumantur' and 'uẽtus' as 'uetus'.

rows.opus_note: Title text agrees (X has the typo 'Oxonienfi'), but X's image description invents 'a harbor with a distant city', while Y describes the engraving more faithfully.
rows.gemini_note: Both transcriptions are equally faithful to the leaf, differing only in markup conventions and the long s in 'Oxonienfi'.

rows.opus_note: X reads the signature 'CC' as 'LL' throughout, repeats 'De saturno in domo martis' in place of 'iouis', and drops 'De Ioue in domo saturni' and the 'CC 5' entry, all of which Y gets right.
rows.gemini_note: X omits 'De Ioue in domo saturni ibidem' and replaces 'De saturno in domo iouis ibidem' with a duplicate 'De saturno in domo martis ibidem'.

rows.opus_note: Nearly identical; X misreads 'cūcta ſcilicet' as 'cūncta ſilicet' and adds italics that are not on the leaf.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'cūcta ſcilicet' as 'cūncta ſilicet'.

rows.opus_note: X matches the hand in 'abstractam', 'eius', 'perspectiva', 'ab aliqua', 'artis' and page '1', where Y has 'abstractionem', 'cuius', 'perspectica', 'alia' and page '20'; Y is better only at 'bene namque ... tam sapiens quamque', where X guesses '<unclear>Utitur</unclear>' and 'quicumque'.
rows.gemini_note: Y introduces corruptions including 'lunt' for 'sunt', 'perspectica' for 'perspectiva', and misreads 'Utitur' as 'bene'.

rows.opus_note: The first line reads 'vincere persta', and Y changes it to 'vincere persas', which brings in Persians that are not on the page; otherwise the two are identical.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads 'persta,' as 'persas,' in line 1.

rows.opus_note: Y follows the print in 'conditio', 'deseri potuisset', 'prope' and 'pagin. 192', where X has 'condicio', 'deferri', 'propè' and '191'; X also normalises v to u ('DUABUS', 'ut').
rows.gemini_note: X gives the wrong page number '191' instead of '192' and misreads 'deseri' as 'deferri'.

rows.opus_note: Y keeps the engraved labels as printed, 'Mediæ Hyerarchiæ attributa' and 'Infimæ hierarchiæ propria'; X reduces them to 'Media Hierarchia attributa' and 'Infima hierarchia propria' and gives the header as 'VIII' elsewhere, but the content is the same.
rows.gemini_note: Y accurately transcribes 'Mediæ Hyerarchiæ' and 'Infimæ hierarchiæ' with the printed ligatures and correctly reads 'Ig 3 nis' and 'A 2 er'.

rows.opus_note: Both have the same text, but Y drops the woodcut D ('E primo ita q; ētel' for 'DE primo itaq; ēte'), misreads it as an 'E', makes up a catchword 'de quid/aut' and has the typo 'potential'.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads slashes as letters creating erroneous words like 'potential' for 'potentia/' and omits the woodcut initial D ('E primo' instead of 'DE primo').

rows.opus_note: Y keeps the printed 'einigermassen', which X normalises to 'einigermaßen', and Y correctly treats 'Inhalt' as a catchword rather than a heading; the wording is otherwise identical.
rows.gemini_note: Both transcriptions are equally faithful, differing only in conventions such as 'einigermaßen' versus 'einigermassen' and the markup for the catchword 'Inhalt'.

rows.opus_note: X misreads 'sperans diuinam opem' as 'qui erant diuinam operam' and 'vtilia dulcibus' as 'vitia dulcibus'; it also has 'Ipe' for 'spe', 'ecudiendæ', 'sensum' and 'nutriant', all of which Y gets right.
rows.gemini_note: X introduces sense-changing errors, transcribing 'vtilia dulcibus' as 'vitia dulcibus' and 'sperans diuinam opem' as 'qui erant diuinam operam'.

rows.opus_note: X has the Greek 'ανομοια' as printed and the catchword 'wer-', where Y has 'ανομια' and 'wers'; the German text is identical.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads the catchword 'wer-' as 'wers' into the body text and transcribes 'ανομοια' as 'ανομια' in the footnote.

rows.opus_note: Y puts most of the body text inside a <margin> tag, writes 'scribit μῆλον potius, quàm μῆλον' where the print has 'βῆλον', garbles the Dutch words ('Fpg', 'Gpf' for 'Vyg', 'Gyf') and leaves out 'luxuriaret'.
rows.gemini_note: Y corrupts the vernacular words ('Fpg', 'foum', 'Gpf' for 'Vyg', 'Voorm', 'Gyf'), misreads Greek 'βῆλον potius' as 'μῆλον potius', and wraps most of the body text in a margin tag.

rows.opus_note: X misreads the definition 'Finis: est id in q̄ principiū q̄escit' as '... desinit', and also has 'bonificādo' for 'bonificās', 'hō'/'rō' for 'vō' and the garbled 'ꝓyelemētatiua'; Y reads all of these correctly.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'q̄eſcit' as 'desinit' in the definition of Finis and garbles 'dꝛ elemētatiua' as 'ꝓyelemētatiua'.

rows.opus_note: The texts are identical except the last line, where the first letter is damaged; X marks it '<unclear>F</unclear>uerit' while Y invents 'Struerit'.
rows.gemini_note: Y invents 'Struerit' in the final line where the leaf reads '<unclear>F</unclear>uerit' and falsely reports a catchword 'huerit'.

rows.opus_note: Y drops 'Diis ipsis loqui solent. Ut apud Livium lib. XXVII, de capta Tarento agens', reads 'lib. xxviii.' for the printed 'XXXVIII.', and appends fragments from the facing page.
rows.gemini_note: Y omits a line ('Diis ipsis loqui solent. Ut apud Livium lib. xxvii, de capta Tarento agens') and includes text from an adjacent leaf.

rows.opus_note: Y matches the labels ('大喜金剛', '北門水藏并身録色', '大捨金剛身録色'), while X gives '大毒金剛', '第三西北毒芥' and '第三北門火前芥身録色'.
rows.gemini_note: X severely misreads multiple inscriptions, transcribing '大喜金剛' as '大毒金剛' and '第二北門水藏把' as '第三北門火前芥'.

rows.opus_note: Y correctly keeps '(Ita. n. arbitrati sunt plurimi)' inline as printed and reads 'deq;', 'præsidi', 'sit', 'asseruerat'; X moves the parenthesis to a margin and has 'dec'', 'prælídí', 'fit', 'assuerat'.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'aſſeruerat' as 'assuerat', 'præſídí' as 'prælídí', and misidentifies page number 3 as 8.

rows.opus_note: X omits whole passages, e.g. 'in vno loco solum. sed maius esset si...' and 'quod deus plura potest facere: quam nullus homo potest intelligere...', and garbles much of the rest.
rows.gemini_note: X omits a substantial passage and margin ('Item sequitur ex dicta regula quod deus plura potest facere...').

rows.opus_note: The texts match, but Y gets the dot patterns for Albus, Puer and Puella wrong (e.g. Albus 'one dot, one dot, two dots, one dot' against the printed oo/oo/o/oo), and it reads 'inuenta' where the page has 'inuentæ'.
rows.gemini_note: Y gives incorrect dot patterns for multiple geomantic figures, describing Albus as '(one dot, one dot, two dots, one dot)' and Puella as '(one dot, two dots, one dot, one dot)'.

rows.opus_note: Both give '康熙三十五年春二月御書' and '一犁杏雨' correctly; they differ only in descriptive notes.
rows.gemini_note: Both X and Y accurately transcribe the calligraphy '一犁杏雨' and inscription '康熙三十五年春二月御書'.

rows.opus_note: Y reads '八蠶獨蛹' and the painting inscription '大繭至八蠶小繭止 獨蛹繭衣繞指柔' correctly; X has '入筐獨蛹', drops a character before '嫗理', and invents the inscription ('大繭糸多小繭糸...').
rows.gemini_note: X invents an inaccurate inscription in the insert ('大繭糸多小繭糸…') and misreads '八蠶' as '入筐'.

rows.opus_note: Y garbles the Greek (e.g. 'ἀνὰ πλέκον' for 'κεφαλὴν μικρὰν'), repeats the line '& fæmine maribus...', and scrambles the margins into the text ('Meleagris ... cur gibbera ... dicta').
rows.gemini_note: Y corrupts Greek passages into nonsensical phrases like 'ἀνὰ πλέκον' and drops text such as 'si de maioribus pennis maxime intelligamus, in Gallopauone'.

rows.opus_note: The texts are nearly identical; Y has '& in centennarys', '& ipz' and 'accidat' (printed 'acci dat') where X has 'zin', 't īpiz' and 'accidens', and Y puts the column break in the right place.
rows.gemini_note: Y is more faithful to the leaf, whereas X introduces OCR errors including 'zin' for '& in', 't īpiz' for '& ipz', and 'ipia' for 'ipsa'.
